reading: A small multi-coloured exemplar sits outside the big rectangles; each single marker cell inside a rectangle gets the exemplar's central 3x3 stamped around it, and lines in the exemplar's arm colour run from the marker to the rectangle's edges along every direction in which the exemplar has an arm beyond its 3x3. The exemplar itself is erased to background.
verb: stamp exemplar and extend its arms

slots.exemplar: the largest multi-coloured component (centre colour = marker colour)
slots.anchors: isolated marker cells of the exemplar's centre colour inside rectangles
slots.pattern: the exemplar's central 3x3, stamped centred on each marker
slots.arms: directions where the exemplar extends past its 3x3; a line of that arm colour runs to the rectangle's edge (not past it)
slots.rest: exemplar cleared to grid background; everything else kept

why: every marker gets the same 3x3 neighbourhood as the exemplar centre, and arm lines fill exactly the marker's row/column inside its rectangle

reading: The number N of 8-cells in the top row is a count; every colour that occurs exactly N times in the patterned row below the 5-separator gets, above its positions, a vertical bar of height N standing on the row just above the separator.
verb: draw bars for colours with count N

slots.N: number of 8 cells in the top-left run
slots.key row: the multi-coloured row below the separator
slots.selected: columns whose key-row colour occurs exactly N times in that row
slots.bars: in each selected column, N cells of that colour directly above the separator

why: bars appear exactly in columns whose key colour has count N, with height N

reading: The single shape is copied four times, rotated by 90 degrees each, and arranged as a cross/pinwheel around an empty centre: the original on the left, its mirror on the right, rotated copies on top and bottom. The output is square with side 2*width + height of the shape.

slots.unit: the bounding box of the one object
slots.copies: left = original, right = left-right mirror, top = 90-degree rotation, bottom = its up-down mirror
slots.size: square of side 2*w + h, centre h x h block empty

why: the four arm blocks are the four rotations of the shape and the centre is background

reading: Two full horizontal and two full vertical 8-lines cut the grid into a 3x3 of panels; the panels are filled by position with fixed colours: top-middle 2, middle-left 4, centre 6, middle-right 3, bottom-middle 1; the four corner panels stay 0.

slots.panels: the 3x3 panels cut by the separator lines
slots.colour map: top-middle 2, middle-left 4, centre 6, middle-right 3, bottom-middle 1, corners unchanged (train constant per panel position)

why: each non-corner panel is uniformly filled with its position's colour on every pair

reading: The 3x3 input shows one colour in one of a few fixed shapes; the output is a single cell whose colour names the shape class (diagonal X pattern -> 2, plus -> 6, the 2x2-block-with-corner pattern -> 3, the zigzag/arrow pattern -> 1), regardless of the input colour.

slots.shape: the binary mask of the 3x3 input (colour ignored)
slots.label: train lookup: mask -> output colour (X->2, plus->6, 011/011/100->3, 110/101/010->1)

why: pairs with the same mask give the same output colour

reading: The colour that occurs most often above the full 5-separator row is written into the centre cell of the bottom row; nothing else changes.

slots.colour: most frequent colour in the rows above the separator

why: exactly one cell changes: bottom-centre gets the majority colour of the top part

reading: The 3x3 input is used as a tile in a 3x3 arrangement of blocks: a block holds a copy of the input exactly where the input cell has the input's most common colour, otherwise the block is empty.
why: every 3x3 block is the input or all 0, and the non-empty blocks are the positions of the input's most common colour
invariants: the unit is the input unchanged

reading: An empty square grid is filled with a clockwise square spiral of colour 3 starting at the top-left corner along the top row, with one background cell between successive turns.

slots.rule: go straight until the next-but-one cell is 3 or the border, then turn clockwise; stop when no move is possible

why: output is the 1-cell-gap spiral for that grid size

reading: A row has a coloured cell at each end; each colour extends toward the other along the row until they meet, and the meeting middle cell becomes 5.

slots.sources: the two end cells on one row
slots.extension: left colour fills the left half, right colour the right half

why: the row between the endpoints is filled half by each colour with 5 at the centre

reading: A two-coloured shape lies on one side of a full 1-coloured separator line; it is reflected across that line (the reflection keeps the original colours), and the original shape's two colours are swapped.
verb: reflect across line and swap colours

slots.copy: mirror image of the shape on the other side, original colours
slots.original: the shape stays in place with its two colours exchanged

why: the far side is the exact mirror of the input shape, and the near side is the input shape with colours a<->b
